title: /proc/<pid>/maps、smaps 与 native 内存映射全貌
key_conclusions: maps is the process mapping catalog, while smaps is the per-mapping memory bill and smaps_rollup is the fast process summary.
Native memory attribution should first land on mapping classes such as heap, anon mmap, ashmem, memfd, stack, code, file-backed mappings, and dalvik spaces.
PSS, Private_Dirty, RSS, Shared_Clean, Swap, and SwapPss deltas are more useful than virtual Size when diagnosing real memory pressure.
Mapping names narrow the investigation but do not prove ownership; HPROF, heapprofd, malloc_debug, fd, dmabuf, thread dump, or source paths are still required.
shallow_points: The article does not include real before/after maps and smaps snapshots from a device.
It does not validate smaps field availability, naming, and permissions across Android versions, SELinux policies, user/userdebug builds, or vendor ROMs.
It does not provide a parser that computes per-mapping deltas between before and after snapshots.
It introduces ashmem, memfd, and dma-buf owner boundaries but leaves detailed shared-buffer accounting to later topics.

Day 30's DirectByteBuffer split appears as a Java wrapper in HPROF and native bytes in heap, anon, or mmap mappings.
Day 28's procrank/showmap ranking becomes actionable only after mapping deltas identify which owner tool to use.
